steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl.

Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar in a mixing bowl with an electric mixer until smooth. Mix in eggs, one at a time, then stir in vanilla. Add flour mixture and beat just until incorporated. Stir in chocolate chips until evenly distributed. Drop heaping teaspoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto the ungreased baking sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges begin to turn golden, 12 to 15 minutes. Allow cookies to cool for a few minutes on the baking sheets before removing to wire racks to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Ultimate High-Altitude Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This high-altitude chocolate chip cookie recipe has been perfected for baking in upper elevations. No more flat, stiff, and tasteless cookies!
raw_recipe.name: Ultimate High-Altitude Chocolate Chip Cookies

review.reviewBody: I've lived in Colorado 20 years - this is the ONLY chocolate chip cookie recipe that still tastes like "toll house", but works at our altitude. Thank you!!!

These turned out pretty well. They're the first chocolate chip cookies I've had come out since I moved from 4500' to 6600'. I added 3/4 tsp baking powder and 1.5 tsp cornstarch just out of desperation for my cookies not to spread, even with all the extra flour in this recipe. I browned the butter and let it chill in the fridge until almost firm before making the cookies, and allowed the dough to chill all day in the fridge before baking. I used a cookie scoop #40--which is about 2 Tbsp--and they baked in 11-12 minutes (did not flatten dough balls).

I'm at +-5000 ft and this recipe works fine. Using my cookie scoop I consistently get 4 dozen cookies. I don't modify it at all though I can see how people get such a wide variety of results. Cookies, especially at altitude, are sensitive to moisture and sugar content. You may need to modify even this 'high altitude' recipe depending on your specific altitude and humidity. Realistically, there is no "one cookie fits all" high altitude recipe; it would be helpful if authors always specified their original altitudes to make adjustments easier to guess. Fixes for overspreading can include refrigerating the dough before baking and using cool pans, adding extra flour a tablespoon at a time, decreasing the sugar by a few tablespoons, adding extra liquid (like an extra egg), and/or increasing the temperature 10-15 degrees and shortening the cooking time. I've started weighing my flour instead of measuring with a scoop with 120 g= 1 cup. Since doing this I start with the same amount every time and can increase it with precision to the right consistency for my conditions. I found I get the best texture if I bake just till the very edge begins to brown and the rest looks under-baked. Then I take them out and let them finish baking on the pan for about 5 minutes before transferring to a cooling rack. If I let them bake till they look done in the oven, they are overcooked and turn crispy. Keep a slice of bread in the container with the cookies to keep them soft.

Great recipe, I live in Denver suburb. The only changes I made was 1-1/2 tsp salt; and 1-1/2 c. chocolate chunks; and since I have never done any gluten free baking I used 1-3/4 c brown rice flour and 1-3/4 c white whole wheat flour. I have only a hand mixer so used it to blend up butter, sugars, eggs and vanilla. Then mixing in the flour mix by hand was challenging to incorporate all but kept at it. I had to sprinkle in a tsp. of milk to get all the flour absorbed. With 1/3 dough added some chopped pecans, 1/3 dough added dried unsweetened cherries and 1/3 dough chocolate chunks only. My oven is a bit on the cool side so I had to adjust by bumping up temp to 355. Parchment paper is the only way to go on pans. These turned out perfectly (the way I like) with crunch on the outside and chewy on the inside. The brown rice flour adds an interesting texture too.

I'm at 5300 feet. This recipe is perfect as-is in my oven. I did have to alter it slightly for my sister's oven (5200 feet, convection oven): 3/4 tsp baking soda, 3 3/4 cups flour, decrease oven temp to 325, place dough on a pre-heated stone, still bake for 10-12 minutes. In my opinion, better than Nestles Toll House cookies baked at lower altitude. Melt-in-your-mouth, much better!

These turned out GREAT! I live in Flagstaff, Arizona at 7,000 feet and have been searching for the perfect high altitude cookie with no luck until now. They had great flavor and the texture was crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside. I did make some changes. I increased the brown sugar to 1 1/2 cups and reduced the white sugar to 1/2 cup. I also swapped the baking soda with baking powder. One last change, I baked them at 425 for 10 minutes.

This is the easiest recipe I have used in the last 15 years and is now my favorite!
I live at 8000 feet high and have learned these cookies come out fluffy and soft. I bake them at 375 for 15 minutes as I found 350 for 15 minutes is not hot or enough. I also use 1/2 to 3/4 cup more of chocolate chips to compensate for the fluffiness. I will be making this recipe from now on and plan on making lots of people happy cookie eaters.

I made a half recipe, using two eggs instead of 1.5 eggs, which added more moisture than the original recipe. I cooked them in two batches of 12. The first batch of 12 came out very poor - dry, hard and lacking in flavor, with an abundance of baking soda on the palate. We're going to save them and put them in a food processor for a cookie crust or something. I fixed the second batch by adding another .25 tsp of salt (so, triple the amount), a whole tsp of vanilla extract, and .25 tsp of apple cider vinegar (which helps with leavening at high altitude and I figured it would react to cut through some of the baking soda flavor), then re-mixed it. I also baked the second batch at 375 F for 11 minutes. They came out as good as any cookies I've made at 1,500 feet. For reference, we're at about 5,500 feet.

For a slightly less cakey, ever so slightly more gooey cookie I use 1/4 cup less of flour and sub a 1/4 cup of butter for Crisco (so so worth the calories and fat in this recipe) I also use half milk chocolate chips and half semisweet. Make sure your butter and eggs are room temp! Perfect for Colorado Springs baking. This recipe is scrumptious! With a family of four, the cookies are gone in a few hours at most. Every time I make these people ask for the recipe, and can't stop praising them. Delicious!.

This recipe is fantastic! I wrote the changes from this recipe into my Betty Crocker Cook Book Binder. When I moved here at 6300 feet elevation, my chocolate chip cookies, from my old recipe, turned out flat and gummy. These cookies are better than any I made at sea level! They stay puffed up and fluffy and the softness last a few days, (whenever the cookies actually last that long). I have been using this same recipe for a few years now. People are offering to buy them from me! 

Toast 1/2 cup pecans or walnuts in a skillet before mixing the dough and let them cool, then add them at the time you add the chocolate chips. You will be in Cookie heaven!

Worked like a charm in Aurora Colorado (5,471 feet). Best chocolate chip cookies I've had since I moved to Colorado. Thank you!

9/14/14 Edit: I cut the in half and doubled the vanilla (as i have done for every cookie recipe I've ever tried). After baking one batch, which turned out wonderful, I rolled the rest of the dough in to 1 inch balls, placed them on a cookie sheet, and froze them. A couple hours later, after they were frozen, I moved them to a plastic bag and put them back in the freezer. From frozen to perfect cookie took 17 minutes in my 350? oven. Fresh baked cookies to order whenever I want them. I just cannot get over how delicious I find these cookies: the perfect crisp on the outside, chewy in the middle. Again, my compliments.
They turned out perfect!!! Great texture and flavor.
I have made these many times, though I lower the temp by 15 degrees, and get asked for them often! They always turn out great!
Amazing cookings at 9400' of elevation!!

6,500 ft in Colorado Springs: used mini choc chips, light brown sugar, and baked 15min. Turned out just like the picture! They don't taste like tollhouse, BUT the recipe works and they taste like bakery cookies! For those who struggle, try an oven thermometer and do a test cookie first. Good luck!

Originally from near sea level, I now live at 5700’. I’ve used my old recipes, adjusting for the altitude. Good results. Made a single batch of this recipe. I split it into one; chocolate w/mint white chips, the other as is, with Christmas (white) chips. I live in a camper & bake w/a 2022 Emeril 360 air fry oven. Baked the first batch (one tray of each flavor) for the suggested time. They looked puffy yet spread out slightly, and were very crispy, almost hard. Not my style, but good. Second oven load were baked a little less. Chocolate was good, regulars had raw centers, flat as can be. The last batch were cooked even less, but came out decently cooked, and pretty tasty. They still satisfied my sweet tooth. The learning continues… 12/12/24 I just added another star. I left the cookies to cool overnight on the rack. I had the second half of one of the first baked (hard, crunchy, & barely breakable, out of the oven). Amazingly, they had a really nice chew! They call to me from the plastic container (the kind w/4 tabs, only 2 are clipped). Will definitely make again. 😋

I baked them for 13 minutes. They came out really crunchy. I prefer soft cookies.
Colorado Native here! First time I used this recipe. My cookies turned out great! Will save this recipe for the future.
